intro_html: A seller wants one number: what do I walk away with? Dossie's net sheet gets there without a spreadsheet — sale price, commission percentage, and option fee credit pull straight from the contract Dossie already scanned, and the handful of numbers that never live on a contract (mortgage payoff, escrow fee, title policy, HOA transfer fee) are yours to drop in.

steps.h: 1. Open Net Sheet from the Offers section
steps.p: Inside any seller-side dossier, click Net Sheet — sale price, commission percentage, and option fee credit are already filled in from the scanned contract.

steps.h: 2. Add what isn't on the contract
steps.p: Mortgage payoff, escrow and closing fees, title policy, HOA transfer fee, home warranty reimbursement, survey cost, agreed repairs — the numbers only the agent has, entered once.
Dossie totals every deduction and credit into a line-item breakdown ending in Estimated Net Proceeds — then Print / Download hands the seller a clean copy.

callout: Every net sheet is an estimate, not a closing figure — actual numbers settle at the closing disclosure. But it's the same math, done before the seller has to ask.
cta_title: Answer "what do I walk away with" in one click.
cta_sub: Dossie calculates a full seller net sheet from the scanned contract plus a handful of your own numbers — built for Texas agents.

faq.q: What does Dossie pre-fill on the net sheet automatically?
faq.a: Sale price, commission percentage (when a listing agreement was scanned), and the option fee credit — all pulled from the contract Dossie already read. Everything else — mortgage payoff, escrow fee, title policy, HOA transfer fee, home warranty reimbursement, survey cost, agreed repairs — isn't on a TREC contract, so it's entered manually.

faq.q: Is the net sheet a guaranteed closing figure?
faq.a: No — it's an estimate built for planning conversations with the seller. The actual net proceeds are finalized on the closing disclosure at settlement.

faq.q: Can I give the seller a copy?
faq.a: Yes — Print / Download opens a clean, formatted version of the net sheet ready to print or save as a PDF.

faq.q: Does the net sheet work for buyer-side dossiers?
faq.a: Net sheets are a seller-side tool — they live in the Offers section of listing dossiers, since that's where "what do I net" is the seller's question, not the buyer's.
